statement:
For all integers $q\ge 2$ and $d\ge 1$, letting $n=q(d+1)-1$, every continuous map $f:\Delta_n\to\mathbb{R}^d$ has points $x_1,\ldots,x_q$ lying in $q$ pairwise disjoint faces of $\Delta_n$ such that
\[
f(x_1)=f(x_2)=\cdots=f(x_q).
\]
completeness_reason: All q>=2,d>=1 and all continuous simplex maps are quantified.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Disjoint-face coincidences are a topological Tverberg assertion, not a finite feasibility test. Non-prime-power obstruction is a known-theorem lead, not independently cleared here; no new full-scope construction.

statement: Let $V$ be a real Banach space of dimension $m$, with $1<133<m$, such that all $133$-dimensional subspaces of $V$ are isometric to one another. Must $V$ be a Hilbert space?
completeness_reason: Finite real Banach dimension m>133 and universal subspace-isometry hypothesis are explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: A single exceptional dimension does not bound ambient dimension or reduce to finitely many norms. No tractable full-scope rigidity argument identified.

statement: Let $C$ be a simple arrangement of great-circles. The expected size of the $(\le k)$-level is at most $16e\,(k+2)^2$ when the south pole is chosen uniformly at random among the cells of $C$.
completeness_reason: Level, size and the cell-based pole convention require the report; k domain is omitted.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Uniform cells differs from uniform area. A sampling argument must preserve that distribution and the exact constant; cannot certify from a generic arrangement bound.

statement: Suppose a simplicial 4-polytope $P$ with $n$ vertices has the property that, among every three vertices, at least two of them are joined by an edge. Does it follow that the graph of $P$ contains a “large” complete subgraph, say, of size $n/10$?
completeness_reason: Large and say n/10 leave exact intended constant and rounding unsettled.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Alpha(G)<=2 alone supplies only Ramsey bounds, not a linear clique. A counterexample must be realizable as a simplicial 4-polytope; arbitrary dense graphs do not suffice.

statement:
The report states that
\[
R_{n,n+1,d}=k[x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n]/\langle \ell_1^d,\ell_2^d,\ldots,\ell_{n+1}^d\rangle
\]
fails the Weak Lefschetz Property in the cases
\[
(n,d)\in\{(5,5),(7,3),(9,2),(9,3),(11,2),(11,3)\},
\]
where the \(\ell_i\) are general linear forms in the report’s setup.
completeness_reason: Field characteristic and general-linear-form setup are explicitly external.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Six finite pairs look computable via graded multiplication ranks, but a specialized rank defect alone cannot establish generic failure. Literal reports an existing result; no credit route.

statement:
Let \[1m$(I_n)_{n
en1}$\[0m be a \[1mSym-invariant chain of Artinian ideals\[0m. Decide whether either \[1m$I_n$\[0m has the SLP/WLP for all \[1m$n\gg0$\[0m or \[1m$I_n$\[0m does not have the SLP/WLP for all \[1m$n\gg0$\[0m.
completeness_reason: Sym-invariant chain and coefficient field are unspecified; SLP/WLP are two distinct alternatives.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Eventual truth needs uniform control of multiplication ranks along the chain. Fixed-n checks cannot settle either property for every large n; corrupted formatting retained.

statement:
Let $f$ be a Gaussian stationary process over $\mathbb{R}$ with spectral measure $\rho$ having a continuous positive density on $\[-a,a]$ for some $a>0$. For every $\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, the persistence exponent
$$\theta_\rho^\ell:=-\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\log\mathbb{P}\!\left(\inf_{t\in[0,T]}f_\rho(t)>\ell\right)$$
exists.
completeness_reason: Sample regularity/version and whether infinite exponents are allowed are unstated.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Positive density near zero does not itself supply a stated path regularity hypothesis. Persistence needs continuous-time estimates and limiting subadditivity; no bounded certificate route.

statement: For the ant process on an arbitrary finite graph $G=(V,E)$ with distinguished nest and food vertices $N$ and $F$, using the loop-erased or uniform-geodesic reinforcement rule described in the report, does the proportion of ants that travel from $N$ to $F$ along a geodesic tend to $1$ as time tends to infinity?
completeness_reason: Both reinforcement transition rules and convergence mode depend on the report.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Finite graphs still have evolving unbounded weights. Need exact rule and almost-sure versus probabilistic convergence; simulating a few graphs would not decide all graphs.

statement: Are there compact, 4-dimensional examples of non-integrable almost complex structures $J$ with $h_J^- \ge 2$ other than those arising from [3, Proposition 3.21]? In particular, are there any examples with $h_J^- \ge 3$?
completeness_reason: h_J^- and especially exclusion of Proposition3.21 require its actual construction.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Existential example needs nonintegrability and cohomology dimension plus proof of exclusion from that family; overlaps next row and cannot count twice.

statement: Are there compact, 4-dimensional examples of non-integrable almost complex structures $J$ with $h^-_J \ge 2$ other than the ones arising from [3, Proposition 3.21]?
completeness_reason: Unidentified [3] Proposition3.21 is essential to what examples are excluded.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Contained in the first clause of 402882. No independent example beyond the excluded construction established; duplicate scope retained in literal coverage.

statement: Does every c.e. theory $T$ have a globaliser? Yes. For every c.e. theory $T$, there exists a c.e. theory $U$ such that, for every c.e. theory $S$, $S$ is locally interpretable in $T$ if and only if $S$ is interpretable in $U$; Cheng and Pakhomov state that their theory $R(T)$ has this property.
completeness_reason: Every c.e. T and S and the local/global interpretability equivalence are explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Literal itself attributes an affirmative R(T) construction. Treat as reported known, not a new existence proof; actual dependency body unaudited.

statement: Is it the case that, for some natural test sets $T$, there is a proof-search algorithm $(A,P)$ that is $\\succeq$-maximal among all proof-search algorithms, where $(A,P)\\succeq(B,Q)$ means that, for every test set $T$, $\\operatorname{time}_A(\\tau)\\leq\\operatorname{time}_B(\\tau)^{O(1)}$ for all $\\tau\\in T$?
completeness_reason: Natural test sets is undefined and existential T conflicts with universal T in the preorder.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Fixing a finite or easy test set can trivialize an altered question. Cannot replace naturality or the quantifier order with a convenient version.

statement: In the setting of Theorem 4, for every real $\b1>1$, an $\b1$-immersion of $G_{\Delta}^{\diamond}$ may admit several possible central points after the cube move, but the number of such potential central points is conjectured to be at most $3$.
completeness_reason: Theorem4 graph, alpha-immersion and central-point conditions are absent.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: At most three suggests elimination of an algebraic central-point equation, but degree and admissibility inequalities are unknown. No justified polynomial bound or computation.

statement: For every $r\ge 0$, provide a metric on the space $S(V)$ of discrete-time adapted processes evolving in a linear space $V$ that induces the adapted topology of rank $r$, $\tau_r$.
completeness_reason: S(V), rank topology, horizon and topology on V are not defined.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: A metric on actual processes can fail separation when the topology identifies laws. Must settle quotient and state-space assumptions before a metric construction.

statement:
For every $r\ge 0$, the map
\[
\mathcal S(V)\times\mathcal S(V)\to[0,\infty),\qquad (X,Y)\mapsto\left\|S_{r+1}\bigl(\operatorname{Law}(\hat X^r)\bigr)-S_{r+1}\bigl(\operatorname{Law}(\hat Y^r)\bigr)\right\|_{\mathcal T_{r+1}}
\]
is a semimetric on $\mathcal S(V)$ that induces the adapted topology of rank $r$, $\tau_r$.
completeness_reason: Iterated prediction, signature maps, tensor norm and rank topology are external.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: A norm difference gives a pseudometric formally, but inducing precisely tau_r requires injectivity and convergence theorems. The formal triangle inequality is only a helper.

statement:
For every reduced bounded-variation path \(\gamma:[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^d\), the conjectured isometry is
\[
\|\gamma\|_{1\text{-var}}=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\bigl\|n!X^n_{0,T}\bigr\|^{1/n},
\]
where \(X^n_{0,T}\) is the \(n\)-th level of the signature \(S(\gamma)_{0,T}\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) is the projective norm (on the relevant tensor powers induced by the norm on \(\mathbb{R}^d\)).
completeness_reason: Universal reduced bounded-variation paths, signature levels and projective norm are specified.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: The upper bound follows the usual factorial variation estimate; the equality requires a matching asymptotic lower bound for every reduced path. Polygonal cases do not settle scope.

statement: Axially symmetric stationary steady states have been studied numerically, see for instance [27, 1], and constructed [24], but the problem of their stability remains largely open.
completeness_reason: No equation, class of steady states or stability topology is given.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: A research-program sentence cannot define a universal stability theorem; no missing-scope replacement.

statement: The extension of [14] beyond spherical symmetry and linearization is a deeply challenging and wide-open problem.
completeness_reason: Reference[14] is unidentified and no target stability assertion is stated.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Beyond symmetry and linearization does not specify a PDE, norm, perturbation class or quantifiers. No literal theorem to certify.

statement: Let $R_n$ be the adjacency matrix of a uniformly random $d$-regular directed graph on $n$ vertices, equivalently a uniformly random $n\times n$ $0/1$ matrix having exactly $d$ ones in every row and every column. Vu’s conjecture asserts that, for every sequence $d=d_n$ satisfying $3\le d_n\le n-3$, $\mathbb{P}\{R_n\text{ is singular}\}\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$.
completeness_reason: All degree sequences 3<=d_n<=n-3 and the uniform regular matrix model are explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Fixed-degree or dense-degree estimates need uniform bridging across intermediate regimes. A finite singular matrix is irrelevant to a vanishing-probability statement.

statement:
For all integers $n,d\ge 2$ and all choices of $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$, the matrix
\[
\left\{\prod_{i=1}^{d}\frac{1+\cos(x_{j,i}-x_{k,i})}{2}-\frac{1}{n}\right\}_{j,k=1}^{n}
\]
is positive semidefinite.
completeness_reason: All integers n,d>=2 and all n real d-vectors are explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Primary report pp403-405 already states and proves exactly this matrix PSD claim: M is the Schur product of half-angle cosine Gram matrices and M circle M >= J/n. Excluded as source-proved, no novelty inference needed.
primary_coverage: report pp403-405, conjecture and proof application read

statement: Conjecture: Theorem 4 should also hold for closed, connected, smooth manifolds of dimension at least 5 with odd-order abelian fundamental group that are spin, p-atoral for every prime p dividing the order of the fundamental group, and have vanishing \b1-invariants; namely, such a manifold admits a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.
completeness_reason: Corrupted b1-invariants and p-atoral condition need Theorem4 definitions.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Positive scalar curvature requires surgery/index obstruction control for the full spin class. Vanishing an unspecified invariant cannot justify an adaptation from a nonspin theorem.

statement: Let $G$ be a RFRS group of type $\mathrm{FP}_n(\mathbb{Q})$. Then $G$ admits a finite-index subgroup $H$ and an epimorphism $\phi:H\to\mathbb{Z}$ with kernel of type $\mathrm{FP}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ if and only if $\beta_i^{(2)}(G)=0$ for every $i\le n$.
completeness_reason: For RFRS groups of type FP_n(Q), both finite-index fibering and all i<=n vanishing are explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Both implications require homological finiteness of kernels, not merely an epimorphism to Z. Known virtual-fibering theorem lead remains unchecked; no short independent route.

statement: Are there 4-dimensional closed, orientable, smooth manifolds $M$ with $\operatorname{Diff}_0(M)$ not uniformly perfect?
completeness_reason: Existence among closed orientable smooth four-manifolds and Diff_0 is explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: A witness needs unbounded commutator length in the identity component, not merely nontrivial abelianization elsewhere. No suitable quasimorphism identified.

statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$. Then $P\trianglelefteq G$ if and only if $p\nmid\chi(1)$ for every irreducible constituent $\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}((1_P)^G)$ of the induced permutation character $(1_P)^G$.
completeness_reason: Every finite G, prime p and Sylow P with all induced constituents is explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Normal P makes constituents factor through G/P, giving the easy direction. Converse requires a character-theoretic detection mechanism; one direction or small groups are helpers only.

statement:
Let $\rho=(k,k-1,k-2,\ldots,2,1)\vdash n$ be a staircase partition. Then
\[
D_{\mathbb C}(\rho)\otimes D_{\mathbb C}(\rho)=\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n} g(\rho,\rho,\lambda)D_{\mathbb C}(\lambda),
\]
with multiplicity $g(\rho,\rho,\lambda)\ne 0$ for all partitions $\lambda$ of $n$.
completeness_reason: D_C(rho) representation convention and k domain are not explicitly defined.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Universal Kronecker positivity across every partition at every staircase size has no small full-scope certificate. Character-table instances cannot establish the conjecture.

statement: In 2007 it was conjectured that the Constraint Satisfaction Problem (CSP) over a constraint language $\Gamma$ is tractable if and only if $\Gamma$ is preserved by a weak near-unanimity (WNU) operation. After many efforts and partial results, this conjecture was independently proved by Andrei Bulatov and Dmitriy Zhuk in 2017.
completeness_reason: Domain finiteness and core/idempotence conventions of Gamma and WNU are missing.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Literal expressly reports a 2017 proof. Even after restoring finite-domain hypotheses this is a known result, not an eligible adaptation.

statement: Theorem 1. Suppose that, for each vortex component, the initial vorticity satisfies $W_{2}\!\left(\frac{\omega_i^0}{\lambda_i},\delta_{X_i^0}\right)\lesssim\varepsilon$ and $\|\omega_i^0\|_{L^p}\lesssim\varepsilon^{-\gamma}$, with $\gamma=2\left(1-\frac{2}{p}\right)$. Then estimate (5) holds for every $t\in(0,T)$ for some $T\gtrsim1$.
completeness_reason: Estimate(5), dynamics, p range and vortex separation hypotheses are missing.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Theorem-labelled fragment cannot be assessed without the target estimate. Numerical vortex checks would not fill that gap.

statement:
Prove that
\[
G(u,\Omega)=F_0(u,\Omega)
\]
for every $u$ such that $\nabla^\perp u$ is a weak solution to (3) with finite entropy production.
completeness_reason: G,F_0, domain class and equation(3) are undefined.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Equality of relaxation/entropy functionals needs both inequalities under exact boundary assumptions. No independent bounded computation or complete route.

statement: Can degenerate variational integrators (DVIs) be generalised to arbitrary order, using, e.g., Galerkin or Runge–Kutta discretisations of the Lagrangian?
completeness_reason: DVI definition, allowed degeneracy and order conditions require source.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: High-order composition may destroy the degeneracy that removes parasitic modes. Generic integrator order-raising is not a full-scope DVI construction.

statement: The report recalls the question of representing solutions of the gravitational $N$-body equations by convergent series. It states that this question was solved for $N=3$ by Sundman and for $N\ge 3$ by Qiu-Dong Wang: each solution admits a series expansion convergent for all $t$ in its maximal interval of existence.
completeness_reason: Collision treatment and meaning of convergent series in physical versus reparametrized time are unclear.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Literal attributes prior Sundman/Wang solutions. Restoring the correct formulation would be a wording/source correction, not a new result.

statement:
There exists an $\mathcal O[\Delta_Q]$-algebra homomorphism
$$R_{S\cup Q}\longrightarrow T_{S\cup Q,Q\text{-aug}}(K_0(Q)/K_1(Q))_{\mathfrak n_{1,\alpha}}$$
that maps the characteristic polynomial of $\rho_{S\cup Q}(\operatorname{Fr}_v)$ to $P_v(X)$ for every $v\notin S\cup Q$.
completeness_reason: All deformation/Hecke objects, auxiliary data and compatibility hypotheses are absent.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Existence of the displayed homomorphism is not testable from symbol names. The characteristic-polynomial clause alone cannot construct a map.

statement:
Suppose $k$ is discretely valued. If $V/F$ is a projective homogeneous space over a connected linear algebraic group $G/F$, then
\[
V(F)\neq\varnothing \iff V(F_v)\neq\varnothing \text{ for all discrete valuations } v \text{ on } F.
\]
completeness_reason: Relationship of F to discretely valued k is not stated.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Local-global principles over function fields need the exact base-field and valuation setup. Reading it as arbitrary F would change the problem.

statement:
Let $A$ be a complete equicharacteristic regular local ring, with residue field $k$ and fraction field $K$. Then, for every reductive $A$-group scheme $G$, there are canonical isomorphisms
\[
G(k)/R \cong G(A)/R \cong G(K)/R.
\]
completeness_reason: All complete equicharacteristic regular local A and reductive A-group schemes are quantified.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Comparison across residue, ring and fraction field needs R-equivalence specialization and lifting; no uniform elementary bridge identified. Small split groups do not suffice.

statement: Characterize the algebraic groups $G$ such that, for every algebraic group $H$, the functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{gp}}(G,H)$ is representable.
completeness_reason: Base field, category and representability category are not specified.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Hom representability depends on whether schemes, group schemes or finite-type algebraic groups are allowed. No classification can be promoted until this is fixed.

statement: Does there exist an arithmetical enumeration degree $a$ such that, for every $n\in\omega$, the $n$-th skip of $a$ is not below the $(n+1)$-st skip of $a$? Equivalently, is there an enumeration degree $a$ such that every finite skip of $a$ is nontotal?
completeness_reason: Skip operation and its totality convention are external; equivalent clause drops arithmetical.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: An infinite sequence of nontotal skips needs a uniform priority construction, not a single degree or finitely many jumps. No bounded witness route.

statement: Given a 2-c.e. set $D$ of properly 2-c.e. Turing degree, does there exist a c.e. set $A$ such that $D\nleq_T A$ and, for every c.e. set $W$, if $W\leq_T D$, then $W\leq_T A$?
completeness_reason: Every properly 2-c.e.-degree D, existence of c.e. A, and all c.e. W are explicit.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Requires simultaneous lower-cone inclusion and nonreducibility of D. A finite enumeration cannot decide those requirements; no short construction identified.

statement: For all $\varepsilon>0$, the Weil–Petersson probability that a surface of genus $g$ has $\lambda_1<\frac14-\varepsilon$ goes to zero as $g\to\infty$.
completeness_reason: For each epsilon>0 the WP genus-g small-eigenvalue probability tends to zero.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: This is an asymptotic spectral-gap distribution assertion; fixed-genus calculations are not decisive. Needs geometric/probabilistic bounds uniform in g.

statement: The question remains how to recover the four possible real bitangent counts—$4$, $8$, $16$, and $28$—from tropical bitangent classes and their real lifts.
completeness_reason: No class of quartics, tropicalization assumptions or lifting data is stated.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Recovering four numbers is not a theorem until curve degeneracy and real-lift rules are fixed; no replacement with generic quartics.

statement:
Let $L\subset K^E$ be a realization of a matroid $M$ over an algebraically closed field $K$ of arbitrary characteristic, and let $W_L$ be the associated wonderful compactification. Is
\[
H^i(\det Q_M;W_L)=0
\]
for all $i>0$?
completeness_reason: Wonderful model and det Q_M construction are not defined.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Arbitrary characteristic rules out a casual Kodaira-vanishing argument. Need a characteristic-free positivity or explicit cohomology mechanism for every realized matroid.

statement: The odd components of the minimal strata $\operatorname{P}\Omega \mathcal{M}_{g,n}(2g-2)^{\mathrm{odd}}$ have maximal Kodaira dimension for $g \ge 12$.
completeness_reason: n and marked-point convention are free in the minimal-stratum notation.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: General type requires global pluricanonical/birational constructions for all g>=12, not a low-dimensional count. Markings can change the dimension and assertion.

statement: The Strominger–Yau–Zaslow conjecture, subject to some interpretation, asks for a special Lagrangian $T^n$-fibration at least in the generic region of a Calabi–Yau manifold, where “generic” could be taken to mean an open region containing $0.99$ of the total measure.
completeness_reason: Subject to interpretation and generic region do not specify a single quantified SYZ statement.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Measure fraction alone does not define fibration singularities, metric limit or family. No formal target should be invented.

statement: **Theorem 2.** Let $G$ be a Hermitian group of rank $3$. For every large enough $g \ge 2$, there exists a maximal representation $\rho:\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\to G$ such that $E_\rho:\mathcal T_g\to(0,\infty)$ has at least two stationary points.
completeness_reason: E_rho, maximality normalization and Hermitian-group hypotheses require definitions.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Already labelled Theorem2. Two stationary points require distinct conformal structures, not two parametrizations; existing-result lead rather than a new proof.

statement:
For every compactly supported area-preserving diffeomorphism \(\phi\) of the two-disc \(D^2\), does
\[
\lim_{d\to\infty}\frac{c_d(\phi)}{d}=\operatorname{Cal}(\phi)
\]
hold?
completeness_reason: The c_d spectral invariants and Calabi normalization are not defined.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: All compactly supported area-preserving disc maps require uniform asymptotics; special Hamiltonians or normalization checks are not full scope.

statement: Is the Newhouse phenomenon locally typical? In the germ-typicality sense defined in the report, the answer is affirmative near any surface local $C^r$-diffeomorphism displaying a dissipative bicycle: for every $2\le r<\infty$, there is a nonempty open set whose closure contains the given diffeomorphism and on which the Newhouse phenomenon is $C^r$-germ-typical.
completeness_reason: Germ-typicality and dissipative bicycle are explicitly source-defined.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Literal states an affirmative local theorem. Reproving the stated result would be ineligible; global typicality is a separate stronger question not licensed here.

statement:
Let $N$ be a homogeneous space, and let $D T^*N$ be the unit disc bundle of $T^*N$. Then there exists a constant $C$ such that, for every exact Lagrangian $L$ in $D T^*N$, one has
$$
\gamma(L)\le C.
$$
completeness_reason: gamma invariant, allowed homogeneous spaces and Lagrangian conventions are missing.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: A uniform C for all exact L needs a geometric bound independent of L; scaling and graphs alone do not address arbitrary Lagrangians.

statement: Does every finite group \(G\) occur as a Galois group over \(\mathbb{Q}\), and, more strongly, over \(\mathbb{Q}(t)\) with no constant subfields?
completeness_reason: Every finite group is requested over Q and regularly over Q(t).
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Inverse Galois and regular inverse Galois require arbitrary groups; realizations of families or one group are excluded instances. No short universal construction.

statement:
Let $X/\mathbb{Q}$ be a hyperbolic curve, and let $X$ be a model over $\mathbb{Z}$. Let $n\ge 1$. Then
\[
X(\mathcal{O}_K)=X(\mathbb{Z})
\]
for 100% of primitive number fields $K$ of degree $n$, when ordered by discriminant.
completeness_reason: Primitive-field convention and allowed integral model are not fixed.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Density-one integral-point equality needs counting exceptional number fields and excluding constant/subfield mechanisms. Finite-degree examples do not establish 100 percent.

statement: Conjecture: Aside from the \-adic images known to arise for infinitely many \mathbb{Q}\-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves \$E/\mathbb{Q}\$, the list of 22 exceptional images that arise for any prime \$\$ and any non-CM elliptic curve \$E/\mathbb{Q}\$ is complete.
completeness_reason: Prime variable is lost and the list of 22 images is absent.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Cannot test completeness of an unidentified exceptional-image list; no substitute list or guessed prime convention.

statement: For the instanton numbers defined by the Lambert expansion $K(q)=1+\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{A_nq^n}{1-q^n}$ in the quintic construction, are $a_n=\frac{5A_n}{n^3}$ integers for every $n\ge 1$?
completeness_reason: K(q) and the quintic construction generating A_n are absent.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Lambert expansion alone permits arbitrary coefficients and imposes no integrality. Need the exact mirror-period definition; no coefficient sweep justifies every n.

statement: For every positive integer \(m\), there exist infinitely many simple abelian varieties over \(\mathbb F_2\), of various dimensions, whose groups of \(\mathbb F_2\)-rational points have order \(m\).
completeness_reason: For every positive m infinitely many simple abelian varieties over F2 are required, dimension unrestricted.
quantifiers_and_technical_assessment: Honda-Tate-style construction must enforce irreducibility, Weil bounds and fixed evaluation m uniformly. One polynomial per m or nonsimple products is insufficient; known-result lead unchecked.
